starom: Old Town Square and the Orloj

Prague's medieval heart: the square with the Gothic Týn Church and its two black spires, the Town Hall with the 15th-century Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and the Jan Hus monument. On the hour the twelve apostles parade past the Orloj's little windows.
karlov: The 14th-century Gothic bridge with thirty statues of saints, always full of street artists. Beyond the Tower, the Malá Strana (Lesser Town) quarter has Baroque houses, the Lennon Wall and Kampa Island with its park on the Vltava.
hrad: Prague Castle and St Vitus Cathedral

The largest palace complex in Europe, on the hill above the Vltava: St Vitus Cathedral with its Mucha stained glass, the Old Royal Palace, St George's Basilica and Golden Lane. The courtyards and gardens are free; the buildings need a ticket.
josef: Europe's oldest Jewish quarter, with the 13th-century Old-New Synagogue still in use, the Pinkas Synagogue with the names of 80,000 Holocaust victims and the Old Jewish Cemetery, where the gravestones are layered twelve deep.
vaclav: The long boulevard rising to the National Museum, with the statue of St Wenceslas on horseback: many moments of Czech history happened here, from the 1989 Velvet Revolution on. All around are Art Nouveau buildings and the entrances to the covered arcades of Nové Město.
petrin: The green hill above Malá Strana, with a lookout tower inspired by the Eiffel Tower and a rose garden. Take the funicular from the Újezd stop: the view of the city, the Castle and the river is one of the best.
vysehrad: Prague's second fortress, on a crag above the Vltava: the Basilica of Sts Peter and Paul, ramparts overlooking the river and the cemetery where Dvořák, Smetana and Mucha are buried. Along the river you pass Frank Gehry's Dancing House.
letna: A panoramic park above the Vltava, right where the enormous Stalin statue once stood: today there's a giant metronome, and from the viewpoint you see the bridges, the Old Town and the Castle.
zizkov: The 216-metre television tower, Prague's most debated landmark, with David Černý's ten giant babies crawling up it; in Vinohrady, the greenest neighbourhood, there are Art Nouveau buildings and Riegrovy sady park, with a view over the city.
